one_line_contribution: A pre-registered paired measurement of how much of a retrieved procedural-experience bank's benefit survives once the instruction slot is filled by a GEPA-optimized prompt trained on the same 800 episodes, with a family of information-free instructions (H1 evidence-citation, H2 decompose-and-verify, I0+3 extra search budget) used as a level-matched control so that the drop can be attributed to absorption rather than to a ceiling effect; secondary contributions are an own-bank/other-bank provenance crossover with a planted half-specific positive control, and a token-matched compiled block C_ab tested against live retrieval on top of the optimized instruction.
closest_prior_work: Two, in different ways. (a) MIPROv2 (2406.11695) already runs the two-container ablation — instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint, optimized on one training set — and already reports that the split is task-dependent. The proposal concedes this and correctly notes MIPROv2 does not retrieve, distill, hold episodes out across containers, or token-match; but a reviewer will say the conceptual claim (instructions and demonstrations are substitutable containers for the same training signal, in proportions that vary by task) is MIPROv2's finding, and this proposal supplies a query-conditioned read and better statistics rather than a new claim. (b) EvoAgentBench (cited as 2607.05202) is the empirical threat: it already places ReasoningBank and GEPA on the same 528/267 trajectories and on Qwen3.5-27B, one of this proposal's own candidate agents, reporting +3.6 vs +1.2. The proposal's audit of it is honest and the remaining delta is real — no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell, no token matching, no compiled arm, no paired statistics — but that delta is an ablation-grade contribution layered onto an existing table, not a new object of study. I note I cannot independently verify EvoAgentBench, which is a 2026-07 preprint read from a PI-supplied PDF; if its appendix contains any GEPA+memory cell, the contribution collapses to the headroom control alone.
strongest_objection: The confirmatory endpoint is not identified. Delta_abs = g_H(l1) - g(I1_ab, B_ab) assumes memory's gain is a function of no-memory accuracy level alone, so that any instruction at level l1 that carries no episode content predicts what memory should have added. The information-free family cannot support that assumption: H2 ('decompose the question into sub-questions, search each, and verify before finishing') is content-identical to the modal ExpeL/ReasoningBank insight for multi-hop QA, so g(H2, B_ab) is depressed by content overlap; I0+3 is a pure tool-budget change that alters how much evidence is already in context and therefore changes memory's marginal value through a completely different channel; I0 is the un-optimized scaffold. These three points do not lie on one curve indexed by accuracy, and the proposal's own Risk 4 concedes H2's overlap while calling it 'the point'. Worse, the pre-registered primary comparator is not the interpolated curve but the single family member I_H* nearest l1 — and I_H* is selected on S_dev2 at n=300 where the paired gain has SE ~2.4pt by the proposal's own arithmetic. So the headline number depends on which of three qualitatively different one-liners happens, within noise, to land nearest wherever GEPA's accuracy falls; if it is H2 the estimate is biased conservative, if it is I0+3 it is biased anti-conservative, and nothing in the design distinguishes these. The proposal also allows l1 to fall outside the family's range, in which case the confirmatory endpoint is an extrapolation 'reported as a limitation' — a confirmatory endpoint that may be an extrapolation off a three-point curve is not confirmatory. Compounding this, the claim threshold (2pt) sits below the stated MDE (<=2.9pt) and below the treatment-free null floor the proposal itself expects (~2pt at n=1,500), and the G1/G2/G7' gate chain — each with modest power at n=300, where they compute that a true 1pt effect passes G1 only ~10% of the time — makes 'no pairing clears the gates, publish the memory-null report' the modal outcome by the design's own numbers. The likeliest reading of this submission is a rigorous study that never gets to test its title.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Replace the three-point information-free family with a genuine level control that varies one thing monotonically — e.g. search budget swept over 6, 8, 11, 14 calls, or partial adoption of I1_ab's edits — so g_H(l) is estimated at five or more levels that bracket l1, fit with a slope and CI that is propagated into SE(Delta_abs) instead of picking one nearest neighbour on a 300-instance dev sample; keep H1/H2 as secondary points, not as the primary comparator. 2) Add the on-policy bank arm named in missing_baseline. 3) Abandon random 400/400 halves for the crossover: random halves of one pool are exchangeable by construction, the proposal admits Delta_info is expected to be zero in E1, and cells 5/6/11/12/13 spend roughly 24,000 Tier-0 episodes confirming a foregone conclusion. Split instead by structure — bridge vs comparison questions and source dataset in E1, the six ALFWorld task types in E2 — so provenance has something to carry and a null is informative. 4) Make E2 the confirmatory environment rather than a Tier-1 reduced-budget replication: tool-augmented multi-hop QA over a fixed corpus is the domain where procedural memory has least to teach (the whole lesson is roughly H2), so a demonstration of absorption there is close to rigged and least interesting; recurring-subroutine environments are where the answer matters, and the proposal's own Prediction 2 concedes this. 5) Either raise n or move the claim threshold above the MDE and the 95th-percentile null floor, so a pass is not defined at an effect size the instrument cannot resolve. 6) Elevate cell 8 (I2_ab, the instruction co-optimized with the bank) from a 2-seed secondary to a primary arm: the track asks about coupling between a self-editing memory and an optimizer, and this proposal explicitly refuses self-editing (Risk 13) and demotes the only coupling cell — it answers a substitution question the track did not pose while leaving the track's named question to a secondary endpoint.
missing_baseline: An on-policy bank: a bank B^{I1} distilled from training episodes generated under I1_ab (or under each information-free instruction), retrieved at that same instruction. As written, every bank is distilled from episodes the agent ran under bare I0 (screening stage S1: 'run bare I0 on the 800-episode training pool (bank-gen)'), so at I1_ab the bank is off-policy: its INSIGHT/PROCEDURE/OUTCOME items describe traces produced by a different policy with a different step structure and output style. Memory's gain shrinking at I1_ab is then equally explained by bank staleness as by the instruction having absorbed the information, and the two are not separated anywhere in the 23-cell grid. H1/H2/I0+3 only partially control for this, since a one-line handwritten addition perturbs the policy far less than an evolved GEPA instruction, so the policy-shift magnitude is not matched along the headroom curve — which means the confound is largest exactly at the point the primary endpoint is evaluated. Cell 8 (I2_ab) does not cover it: it lets the optimizer see the bank, but the bank is still I0-derived. A secondary omission: an instruction optimized at matched rollout budget on episodes disjoint from the bank's source pool at full data — cell 5 does this only at 400-episode halves, so the title's load-bearing phrase 'optimized on the same episodes' is never tested at the scale the primary endpoint uses.
preprint_collision: The check is well above the norm and should be credited: it is dated (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), states its channels and counts (15 HuggingFace queries, 244 papers, 54 by-id verifications), commits raw scan records with SHA256s, explicitly withdraws v2's sentence that no published work uses one method as the control for the other, and reinstates five citations a previous round had wrongly retracted with a stated procedural rule. Naming EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) as a near-collision and enumerating what it does and does not contain is exactly the right move. Three real weaknesses remain. First, arXiv is unreachable from the node, so nearly every post-2026 ID rests on web-search snippets — and the check itself records that a snippet misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 against the PDF's +3.6. That is direct evidence the verification channel is unreliable, yet the entire related-work map and the motivating numbers rest on it, and the one paper checked properly was checked from a PDF supplied by the PI rather than obtained independently. Second, the appendix of 2608.14036 (skills vs Workflow Memory) is admittedly unopened and is precisely where a token-matched compiled-block-versus-retrieval comparison would live — i.e. where Prediction 4, the compile-once result, would already be scooped; deferring that to a 'pre-freeze re-scan' means the compile contribution's novelty is currently unestablished, not merely unconfirmed. Third, and most telling, the proposal states that the design primitive it leans on hardest — a held-out-episode provenance crossover asking whether an optimizer's gain is specific to the episodes it saw — has never been searched at all and is item (2) on the re-scan list. A novelty claim for the crossover therefore has no search behind it. Note also that I cannot verify any of the 26xx-series IDs myself; I am judging the check's method and self-consistency, not the existence of the papers.
